event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: considered whether deleting the static browser scrollback assertion establishes a current history-retention regression. It does not. Details: the deleted test parses terminal.js's xterm scrollback literal and compares it with tmux::HISTORY_LIMIT. SPEC.md:2962-2963 retains the product floor of the screen plus 10,000 history lines. Host terminals use a different renderer: SPEC_impl.md:1898-1917 states that the browser receives screen/history rows and that a host terminal mounts the grid directly; source terminal.js:32-40 and grid-model.js:792-799 support that distinction. GridModel sets historyCap from the supervisor's hello history_cap, so the removed cross-language xterm/tmux literal comparison does not validate the current host grid cap. Existing service/grid_stream/tests.rs has source assertions for held history across catch-up (:313-332), paused floods (:485-505), full writers (:520-545), and eviction (:560-584). This is source inspection, not an executed pass, and those tests do not independently certify the default 10,000-line floor. No changed runtime cap or route to missing history was established by this deletion. Suggested bucket: other (test-coverage concern). Confidence: confirmed by source regarding test applicability; no runtime observation. proposed_drop: true, source refutation of a product regression attributable to this deleted xterm/tmux bound. possible_cover: none. Could-be-highest: no established loss-of-work route; the considered issue is coverage removal in maintainer tooling, not demonstrated output loss. This is not a specification-accepted product bug.
